notes.1: This measurement question was well answered, with distractor C being the most popular, these candidates failing to notice that there were two rotations of the can.
notes.3: The majority of candidates answered this correctly, although some failed to read that the car had travelled 60 times around the track, so opted for the physically unlikely option A. �PAGE�2
notes.7: The most common misconception was that passengers standing upstairs would lower the centre of mass of the bus.
notes.8: This question concerned equilibrium, and many of the candidates opted for B. Although the two horizontal forces were equal, they acted at different distances from the pivot, so the handle was not in equilibrium.
notes.9: Most candidates knew which of the energy sources were renewable, the main misconception being that nuclear fuels were in this group; it should be stressed that nuclear fuel, although not a fossil fuel, is non- renewable.
notes.10: Options C and D were both quite popular distractors. Candidates needed to realise that the gravitational potential energy of the object will not be zero at Y.
notes.12: This question concerned a manometer; almost a quarter of the candidates added the 8cm difference between the two levels to the atmospheric pressure, instead of subtracting it.
notes.15: The most common error was to select option B, these candidates believing that mass could be affected by temperature.
notes.18: Candidates found this the most difficult question on the paper. Option D was very popular, with candidates apparently confusing evaporation with convection. A significant number chose option C, believing that liquid molecules expand when heated.
notes.20: Although this was a very simple recall question, a large proportion of the candidates could not identify the unit of wavelength.
notes.21: Knowledge of the nature of light waves and radio waves was shown to be lacking here, with over half of the candidates choosing incorrectly. It would be worth reminding candidates that the two columns in a question do not necessarily have to have different contents for a row to be correct.
notes.22: The name of the effect shown (diffraction) was very well known, but there was considerable uncertainty about the effect of gap size on the amount of diffraction which would occur.
notes.23: This question concerned the image formed by a plane mirror. A large majority of candidates were familiar with the fact that the image is laterally inverted and not magnified, but some of these did not appreciate that it is also virtual. �PAGE�3
notes.24: This lens question was well answered, the main misconception being that all refracted rays must pass through the principal focus.
notes.28: A significant proportion of candidates could not recognise a method by which a steel bar could be demagnetised.
notes.29: This was another simple recall question, on the unit for potential difference, and the majority of responses were correct.
notes.30: A significant number of candidates could not identify a resistor of constant resistance from its V–I characteristic.
notes.31: The circuit symbol for a fuse should have been recognised by virtually all candidates, but a significant minority gave an incorrect response.
notes.33: This question required an understanding of the potential divider. Fewer than half the candidates chose the correct response, with the rest opting for A and D in roughly equal numbers.
notes.34: Almost all candidates answered this graph analysis question correctly.
notes.35: A minority of candidates opted for C, being unaware that the magnetised coil could only repel another magnet.
notes.38: This question was about the change in a nucleus following emission of a β-particle. Almost half the candidates chose options A or C, showing confusion over this part of the syllabus. �PAGE�4
notes.general_comments:
Candidates did particularly well on Questions 4, 5, 6 and 26, with almost all choosing the correct response.
The greatest difficulty was found with Questions 8 and 18. Question 38 also caused some problems, with
fewer than half of the responses correct.
